local.h: Thanksgiving Parade to start an hour early
local.b: For the first time in 92 years, the parade steps off at 7:45 a.m. so the broadcast can air before the Bears play the Lions; former Bear Charles Tillman is grand marshal.

local.h: CPS students could lose Google search over AI rules
local.b: Districts that bar popular AI tools in classrooms, like Chicago Public Schools, will lose access to Google search next year. CPS says it has guidelines to help students and teachers use AI safely.

local.h: Denver weighs changes after tough Colfax construction
local.b: The city is considering big changes to how it supports businesses during its next mega-projects.
local.title: Colfax construction wasn’t fun for business. Can Denver do better next time?

local.h: Restaurants adapt to Denver's foie gras ban
local.b: The law takes effect July 1; advocates estimate about 15 Denver restaurants serve foie gras.
local.title: Denver banned foie gras. Restaurants are already adapting

local.h: Big-name Democrats gather in Denver for 'What's Next'
local.b: The conference has taken over Mission Ballroom and blocks of River North, putting the party's biggest questions on display.

local.h: Lakewood officer killed on RTD bus remembered at funeral
local.b: Agent Nicholas Graham was killed in a shootout aboard an RTD bus last week.
local.title: Lakewood Police agent killed in bus shooting remembered at public funeral service

local.h: Mountain View keeps its strong-mayor system
local.b: After months of political drama, a measure to change the town's political structure failed a second time.
local.title: After months of political drama, Mountain View decides to keep things the same

local.h: Denver weighs renters' unions and tougher landlord rules
local.b: Some City Council members are proposing to let renters unionize and strengthen regulations beyond the city's current power to fine landlords for violations.

local.b: The state judicial commission found Judge Draper engaged in 17 instances of misconduct; he called the decision deeply disappointing.

local.h: Raman promises to halve street homelessness before Olympics
local.b: Mayor-elect Nithya Raman says her plan will cut street homelessness by 50% in time for the 2028 Games and end long-term encampments by the end of her first term.

goodnews.h: Original Pantry Cafe reopens with a new mission
goodnews.b: The century-old downtown diner, closed since March 2025, reopens Nov. 19 run by nonprofit Hope the Mission, with all profits going to shelters for unhoused Angelenos and longtime staff returning under a union contract.

local.h: Flatbush collapse fuels anger over pace of development
local.b: Mayor Mamdani says the city is examining 100 other sites tied to the construction companies, as residents say rapid building is displacing longtime neighbors.
local.title: Brooklyn building collapse has residents questioning pace of development

local.h: City Council bans 'surveillance pricing'
local.b: The bill bars companies from setting prices based on personal data like demographics, credit or browsing history, online and in stores.
local.title: NYC Council passes ban on 'surveillance pricing' that relies on personal data

local.h: Feds charge gang members in 2022 killing of 12-year-old
local.b: Prosecutors say members of a Brooklyn gang fired into the wrong car in East Flatbush, killing a 12-year-old boy, after mistaking it for a rival's.
local.title: Feds say gang members killed 12-year-old in East Flatbush drive-by, targeting a rival

local.h: Developer next to Flatbush collapse had flouted city orders
local.b: Buildings department records show the owner of the lot being excavated beside the collapsed building kept demolishing after a stop work order earlier this year and was penalized again.
local.title: Developer at Brooklyn collapse site had record of flouting orders from city agency

local.h: Bill would make delivery apps pay for e-bike fixes
local.b: A City Council bill from Councilmember Harvey Epstein would require food delivery companies to fund fixes for crowded e-bike parking, like the East Village block where hundreds of bikes line the curb.
local.title: NYC bill would require food delivery firms to fund fixes to the e-bike 'crisis'

local.h: New Yorkers line up to become casino dealers
local.b: Big Deal Casino Academy in NoMad, the city's only Education Department-licensed dealer school, is scaling up as New York City's first full-scale casino, in Jamaica, finally arrives.
local.title: A good bet: New Yorkers are lining up to become casino dealers

local.h: Greenpoint street redesign previews 'low-traffic' plan
local.b: New diverters on Driggs Avenue force drivers to turn near McGolrick Park, a model city lawmakers want citywide. A ballot measure passed last week could speed such redesigns.
local.title: North Brooklyn street redesign paves the way for NYC's 'low-traffic neighborhood' plan

local.h: Flatbush building collapse death toll rises to eight
local.b: City officials said Thursday the collapse of a three-story apartment building in Flatbush has killed eight people and injured at least 25, including at least seven children, as crews kept searching the rubble.
local.title: FDNY ends search at Brooklyn building collapse: 6 adults, 2 children dead, 18 injured

goodnews.b: A small study found health care costs fell sharply for homeless patients after NYC Health and Hospitals helped house them, while their spending on preventive care rose.
goodnews.title: Homeless New Yorkers’ healthcare costs plummeted after getting housed, study finds

local.h: Two Britons charged over €16m château fraud
local.b: Prosecutors allege the pair sold investors on a luxury golf development at a château near Limoges; both deny the charges.
local.title: Two Brits charged over €16m French château fraud

local.h: Regulated gas price to rise again in December
local.b: The fourth straight monthly increase will add about €16 to December bills for households on the reference price; fixed-price contracts are unaffected.
local.title: French gas prices to rise for a fourth month in a row in December

local.h: France slams Israel's ban on Melenchon
local.b: Foreign Minister Barrot called the ban on the France Unbowed leader and Mathilde Panot "demagogic" while restating France's push for a two-state solution.
local.title: France slams Israel’s ‘demagogic’ ban on opposition leader Melenchon

local.h: Protests planned across France on Saturday
local.b: Gilets Jaunes list 237 events nationwide, with 30,000 to 60,000 people expected in Paris across three events starting at République.
local.title: MAP: What to expect from France's latest day of protests on November 14th

local.h: France bars prominent Israeli settler leader
local.b: Yossi Dagan was turned back at a Paris airport over his role in West Bank settlement policy, and Israel's foreign ministry said it will demand an explanation.

local.h: French schools hit by hoax bomb threats
local.b: Macron said it was too early to say whether a foreign power was behind the threats, which also reached schools in the UK and Ireland.

local.h: EES glitches leave travellers wrongly accused of overstays
local.b: Several British travellers say the EU's new biometric border system miscounted their 90-day Schengen allowance, leaving some facing travel bans or large fines.

local.h: France to add 70 'medical buses' for rural areas
local.b: The government will deploy 70 more mobile clinics by 2027, bringing the total to 100, to bring GPs and specialists to medical deserts.

local.h: Kirkland weighs raising minimum wage
local.b: The city is considering going above the state's $17.13 minimum after a study of Seattle and other cities' increases.
local.title: Kirkland takes step to raise minimum wage

local.h: Back-to-back atmospheric rivers to soak Northwest
local.b: Two more storms will pound Washington and Oregon Friday and Saturday after two others already dropped inches of rain this week.

local.h: Cracked dock halts ferry trucks to Orcas Island
local.b: San Juan County declared an emergency as groceries arrive by barge and residents hold onto garbage while crews repair cracked steel beams at the terminal.

local.h: AG Brown's office hands trans sports ban defense to outside firm
local.b: Citing potential conflicts, the attorney general appointed national firm Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend voter-passed Initiative 638 in court.

local.h: Council upholds Mayor Wilson's veto on RV permits
local.b: The vetoed rule would have required people living in RVs on city streets to get a permit or risk being towed.

local.h: O'Donnell claims win in WA Supreme Court race
local.b: King County Superior Court Judge Sean O'Donnell leads appeals court Judge Ian Birk by 39,000 votes in the state's closest Supreme Court race.

local.h: Seattle-area PE teachers shrug off revived fitness test
local.b: Schools have largely ignored the new federal fitness test, which isn't mandatory, and many PE teachers say testing makes kids associate exercise with public shame.
